examples.en: A new light rail line opened in our neighborhood.
A light rail runs with smaller trains than the subway.

examples.ko: 경전철 역은 집에서 걸어서 오 분이에요.
examples.en: The light rail station is five minutes from my home on foot.

examples.ko: 경전철은 차량이 작아서 많은 사람이 타기 어려워요.
examples.en: Light rail cars are small, so it's hard for many people to ride.
On the way to the airport I switched to the light rail.

examples.ko: 경전철 공사가 끝나면 교통이 더 편해질 거예요.
examples.en: When the light rail construction ends, getting around will be easier.

explain: '경전철'은 지하철보다 가볍고 작은 전철이에요. 보통 사람이 적은 지역이나 도시 안쪽을 다니고, 지하철과 이어서 탈 수 있어요. 반대로 큰 규모의 지하철은 '중전철'이라고 부르기도 해요.

phrases.en: I take the light rail every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '타다'와 함께 쓰는 가장 기본적인 말이에요. 이용하는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase with 타다 (to ride). Use it when talking about using the light rail.

phrases.example: 우리 동네에 경전철 노선이 새로 생겼어요.
phrases.en: A new light rail line opened in our neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 열차가 다니는 길을 말할 때 써요. 지하철 노선과 비슷하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the route the trains run on, just like a subway line.

phrases.en: The light rail station is a five-minute walk from my home.
phrases.nuance_ko: '경전철'에 '역'을 붙여 정거장을 말해요. 길을 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 역 (station) to 경전철 names the stop. Often used when giving directions.

explain_en: 경전철 is a lighter, smaller train than the subway. It usually runs in less crowded areas or inside a city and connects to the subway. The larger subway-class systems are sometimes called 중전철.

examples.ko: 두 길의 교차 지점에 신호등이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a traffic light at the point where the two roads cross.

examples.ko: 교차 검사를 한 번 더 해 보세요.
examples.en: Please do a cross-check once more.
A crossing section without a signal is dangerous.
I felt joy and sadness mixed together.
Please do a cross-analysis of the voting results.

examples.ko: 교차 확인을 하려고 자료를 두 번 비교했어요.
examples.en: I compared the data twice to cross-check it.

explain: 교차는 두 선이나 길이 만나서 엇갈리는 것, 또는 감정이 번갈아 드는 것에 써요. '교차로(네거리)', '교차 검사'처럼 다른 말과 붙는 경우가 많아요. 길이 만나는 곳을 말할 때 '교차'는 지점, '교차로'는 도로 이름이에요.

phrases.en: Please go slowly at the intersection.
phrases.nuance_ko: '교차'는 만나는 지점이고, '교차로'는 길 자체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 교차 is the meeting point; 교차로 is the road intersection itself.

phrases.en: There is a cafe at the point where the two roads cross.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선이나 길이 만나는 한 점을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The single point where lines or roads meet.

phrases.en: I cross-checked the numbers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 가지 방법이나 자료로 서로 맞는지 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when checking against two methods or sources.

explain_en: 교차 is two lines or roads meeting and crossing, or feelings coming in alternation, and it often joins other words as in '교차로' and '교차 검사'. For roads, 교차 is the point and '교차로' is the intersection itself.

t90.ax: Please do a cross-check once more.

examples.en: To get home, you have to go through the underpass.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 굴다리 아래에 물이 고여요.
examples.en: When it rains, water collects under the underpass.

examples.ko: 갑자기 소나기가 와서 굴다리 밑에서 비를 피했어요.
examples.en: A sudden shower came, so I took shelter from the rain under the underpass.

examples.ko: 이 굴다리는 키 큰 트럭이 못 지나가요.
examples.en: Tall trucks can't get through this underpass.

examples.ko: 저 굴다리 건너편에 큰 시장이 있어요.
examples.en: There's a big market on the other side of that underpass.
At night the underpass is dark, so it's a little scary.

explain: 철길이나 큰 도로 밑을 지나가게 뚫어 놓은 낮은 통로를 말할 때 써요. '육교'가 위로 건너는 다리라면 굴다리는 아래로 지나가는 길이에요.

phrases.en: Let's meet under the underpass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속 장소를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to name a meeting spot.

phrases.en: The bus went through the underpass and entered the town.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차나 사람이 아래 통로로 지나갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a vehicle or person passes through the tunnel.

phrases.en: My house is near the underpass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위치를 알려 줄 때 기준이 되는 장소로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a landmark when giving a location.

explain_en: It is used for a low passage cut through underneath a railway or a big road. If a '육교' (pedestrian overpass) is a bridge you cross over, a 굴다리 is a way you pass under.

t90.ax: Tall trucks can't get through this underpass.

examples.en: It's the weekend, so the market is really teeming with people.

examples.ko: 냄비 속에서 물이 버글버글 끓고 있어요.
examples.en: The water in the pot is bubbling away.

examples.ko: 방학 때 해수욕장은 늘 사람으로 버글버글해요.
examples.en: During vacation the beach is always packed with people.
The morning subway is jam-packed with people, so it's hard.
I can hear the soybean stew bubbling.
On the festival day the square was swarming with people.

explain: 사람이 아주 많이 모여 빽빽할 때와 물이나 찌개가 끓을 때 둘 다 쓰는 말이에요. '북적북적'과 비슷하지만 버글버글은 끓는 모습에도 쓸 수 있어요. '버글버글하다'로도 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: At rush hour the subway station is teeming with people.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-하다'를 붙여 서술어로 쓰고, '~로/으로'와 자주 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-하다' makes it a predicate, often used with '~로/으로'.

phrases.example: 라면 물이 버글버글 끓으면 면을 넣으세요.
phrases.en: When the ramen water bubbles hard, put in the noodles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이나 찌개가 세게 끓는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes water or stew boiling vigorously.

phrases.en: The market is always bustling during the holidays.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 많은 모습만 말하는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word that describes only crowds of people.

explain_en: It is used both when a place is crowded with people and when water or stew is bubbling. It is similar to '북적북적', but 버글버글 can also describe boiling. You can also say '버글버글하다'.

examples.en: In the evening I took a walk along the quay.

examples.ko: 부둣가에 작은 배들이 줄지어 서 있어요.
examples.en: Small boats are lined up along the wharf.
I ate fresh raw fish at a restaurant by the harbor.
A friend and I sat by the pier and watched the sunset.
The wharf is crowded with people from dawn.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 할아버지 댁이 부둣가 근처에 있었어요.
examples.en: When I was little, my grandfather's house was near the wharf.

explain: '부두'의 가장자리, 즉 배를 대는 곳 바로 옆을 말해요. '항구'는 도시나 지역 전체를, '부두'는 배를 대는 시설을 가리켜서 좀 달라요. 쓸 때는 '부둣가에서', '부둣가를 따라'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I saw seagulls at the waterfront.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소를 나타내는 조사 '-에서'를 붙여 쓰는 가장 흔한 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form, with the place particle -에서.

phrases.en: I ate grilled fish at a restaurant by the wharf.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부두 근처에 있는 가게를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for shops located near the wharf.

phrases.en: I walk along the wharf every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산책할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when talking about strolls.

explain_en: It means the area right beside a '부두' (wharf), where ships dock. '항구' (port) refers to the whole harbor town or area, while '부두' is the docking facility. You will hear it as '부둣가에서' or '부둣가를 따라'.

en: to be noisy; to be loud; to be clamorous

examples.en: It's market day, so the neighborhood is buzzing and noisy.

examples.ko: 교실이 시끌시끌해서 선생님이 조용히 하라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The classroom was so noisy that the teacher told us to be quiet.

examples.ko: 명절에는 온 가족이 모여 집안이 시끌시끌해요.
examples.en: During the holidays the whole family gathers and the house is lively and loud.

examples.ko: 소문 때문에 회사가 며칠째 시끌시끌한 분위기예요.
examples.en: Because of a rumor, the company has been in a buzzing uproar for days.
The next-door house was so noisy that I went out to look.

examples.ko: 카페가 너무 시끌시끌하니까 다른 데로 가요.
examples.en: This cafe is too noisy, so let's go somewhere else.

explain: '시끄럽다'는 소리가 불쾌할 때 많이 쓰고, 시끌시끌하다는 여러 사람이 떠들어서 북적이는 느낌이에요. 장날이나 명절처럼 활기찬 곳에도 쓰고, 소문이나 논란으로 어수선한 분위기에도 써요.

phrases.en: I shopped at the lively, noisy market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 많아서 활기찬 곳을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a bustling place full of people.

phrases.en: The children are chattering noisily.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여 여러 사람이 떠드는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -게 it describes many people talking loudly together.

phrases.en: It's a holiday, so the house is lively.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고, 즐겁고 활기찬 분위기에 특히 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning and especially fitting for a cheerful, lively mood.

explain_en: '시끄럽다' is often used when the noise is unpleasant, while 시끌시끌하다 gives the feel of many people chattering and bustling. It fits lively places like a market day or holidays, and also a stirred-up atmosphere caused by rumors or controversy.

t90.ax: This cafe is too noisy, so let's go somewhere else.

examples.ko: 가게 안이 왁자지껄 시끄러워서 대화가 안 돼요.
examples.en: The shop is so boisterous that we can't have a conversation.
The kids came out of the school gate chattering loudly.

examples.ko: 명절이라 온 가족이 모여 왁자지껄 웃고 떠들어요.
examples.en: It's a holiday, so the whole family gathers and laughs and chats noisily.
The market alley is full of boisterous energy.

examples.ko: 학교 앞 분식집에서 학생들이 왁자지껄 이야기해요.
examples.en: Students are talking noisily at the snack shop in front of the school.
The noisy sounds I'd been hearing suddenly went quiet.

explain: 여러 사람이 한꺼번에 떠드는 소리가 크게 들릴 때 써요. '시끌벅적'과 비슷하고, 즐겁고 활기찬 분위기에 자주 어울려요. 뒤에 '떠들다', '웃다' 같은 말이 자주 와요.

phrases.en: There are many people chatting noisily in the restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어와 '떠들다'를 함께 쓴 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing with 떠들다.

phrases.en: My friends came in laughing loudly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 즐겁고 활기찬 분위기로 여럿이 크게 웃는 모습에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits several people laughing loudly in a cheerful, lively mood.

phrases.en: The children are making a racket in the classroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻의 말로, 여럿이 모여 소란스러울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word, used when a group is noisy and bustling.

explain_en: It is used when the noise of many people talking at once is loud. It is close to '시끌벅적' and often fits a cheerful, lively atmosphere. Verbs such as '떠들다' and '웃다' often follow it.

t90.ax: The market alley is full of boisterous energy.

examples.ko: 십오 년 된 차를 이번 주에 폐차해요.
examples.en: I'm scrapping my fifteen-year-old car this week.
The car was so old that I decided to scrap it.

examples.ko: 사고 난 차를 폐차했는데 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: I scrapped the crashed car and it hurt.

examples.ko: 폐차하면 보조금을 받을 수 있는 경우도 있어요.
examples.en: If you scrap a car, you can sometimes receive a subsidy.
My father is cleaning out the car he is going to scrap.
After scrapping the car, I get around by public transportation.

explain: 폐차하다는 차를 완전히 없앨 때 쓰는 말이에요. 차를 팔 때는 '팔다', 새 차로 바꿀 때는 '바꾸다'를 써서 폐차와 구분해요. '차를 폐차하다'는 같은 말이 겹쳐서 어색하니 그냥 '폐차하다'나 '폐차를 하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I'm going to scrap my old car.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 폐차할 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about a plan to scrap a car.

phrases.en: I scrapped my old car last month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 끝난 일을 말하는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense, for something that is already done.

phrases.example: 아직 탈 수 있으니까 폐차하지 마세요.
phrases.en: It still runs, so please don't scrap it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 하지 말라고 부탁하거나 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask or persuade someone not to do it.

explain_en: 폐차하다 is used when a car is disposed of for good. When you sell a car you say '팔다', and when you swap to a new one you say '바꾸다', which separates them from 폐차. '차를 폐차하다' repeats the same word and sounds awkward, so people just say '폐차하다' or '폐차를 하다'.

examples.en: I bought a newspaper at the stand in the subway station.
A street stall opens every morning.
Fruit is piled high on the stall.
The woman at the stand gave me my change.
The socks sold at the stall are cheap.
Once the stalls are cleared away, the street gets wide.

explain: 길이나 역 앞에 임시로 놓고 물건을 파는 작은 판매대예요. 신문, 과일, 양말, 액세서리를 팔 때가 많아요. 가게 안의 '진열대'와 달리 밖에 있는 간이 판매대를 말해요.

phrases.example: 역 앞 신문 가판대에서 잡지를 샀어요.
phrases.en: I bought a magazine at the newspaper stand in front of the station.
phrases.nuance_ko: 파는 물건 이름을 앞에 붙여 어떤 가판대인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the item sold before the word to say what kind of stall it is.

phrases.en: I bought tangerines at a fruit stall by the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길에서 과일을 파는 작은 판매대를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A small outdoor stall that sells fruit.

phrases.en: The man sets up his stall every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 임시 판매대를 설치해서 장사를 시작한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to set up a temporary stall and start selling.

explain_en: It is a small temporary sales stand set up on a street or in front of a station. It often sells newspapers, fruit, socks or accessories. Unlike a '진열대' (display shelf) inside a shop, it is an outdoor makeshift stand.

examples.en: I buy shoes online.
Tickets are cheaper if you buy them in advance.
I purchased a laptop last week.
I wrote the items to buy in a list.
The book I purchased arrived today.
It's on sale, so I'm buying a lot.

explain: 가게에서 말할 때는 '사다'를 훨씬 많이 써요. '구매하다'는 쇼핑몰, 앱, 안내문, 영수증 같은 글에서 자주 보여요. '구매 목록', '구매 후기'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I read purchase reviews before buying.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쇼핑몰에서 많이 보는 명사 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common noun pairing seen on shopping sites.

phrases.example: 이 표는 앱에서 구매할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can purchase this ticket in the app.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어디서 살 수 있는지 안내할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain where something can be bought.

phrases.en: I buy apples at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구매하다'보다 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Much more common in daily speech than 구매하다.

explain_en: In conversation at a shop, the plain verb for buying is far more common. This word is typical of online shops, apps, notices and receipts, and the noun form appears in terms like purchase list and purchase review.

dis.h: buy as a customer, often online
gh: buy a thing, general and neutral
buy goods or land for business

p.n: Almost the same; 구입하다 feels slightly more like buying a thing in person.

examples.en: That company monopolizes the market.

examples.ko: 동생이 리모컨을 독점해서 채널을 못 바꿔요.
examples.en: My little brother hogs the remote, so I can't change the channel.
Give up the idea of keeping all the popularity to yourself.

examples.ko: 한 나라가 자원을 독점하면 가격이 올라요.
examples.en: If one country monopolizes a resource, prices go up.
That singer swept the music charts.
You can't keep all the good seats for yourself.

explain: 시장·권력·기회 같은 큰 것에도 쓰고, 리모컨·대화·인기 같은 일상의 작은 것에도 써요. 혼자만 가지려는 느낌이 강해서 부정적일 때가 많아요. '독차지하다'는 일상 대화에서 더 흔하고, '독점하다'는 뉴스와 경제 글에서 더 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling got all of our parents' love.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '독점하다'보다 더 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common in daily talk than '독점하다'.

phrases.example: 이 가게가 이 상품을 독점 판매해요.
phrases.en: This shop sells this product exclusively.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 곳만 팔 수 있는 상황을 말하는 경제 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An economic phrase for when only one seller can sell it.

phrases.example: 한 사람이 대화를 독점하면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: One person shouldn't monopolize the conversation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 혼자만 계속 말하는 사람에게 쓰는 부정적인 느낌의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative phrase for someone who keeps talking alone.

explain_en: It works for big things such as markets, power and opportunities, and for small everyday things such as the remote, a conversation or popularity. It often carries a negative feeling of keeping everything to yourself. 독차지하다 is more common in daily talk, while 독점하다 appears more in news and economics.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 내 돈을 떼어먹고 이사 갔어요.
examples.en: He stiffed me for my money and moved away.
You must not cheat people out of their money.
I'm worried the client will skip out on the payment.

examples.ko: 회비를 떼어먹은 친구와는 더 이상 안 만나요.
examples.en: I don't see that friend anymore, the one who ran off with the membership fees.

examples.ko: 임금을 떼어먹는 가게에서는 일하고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to work at a shop that stiffs workers on their wages.

examples.ko: 외상값을 떼어먹지 말고 이번 달에 꼭 갚으세요.
examples.en: Don't dodge the tab; make sure you pay it this month.

explain: 빚, 외상값, 임금처럼 갚아야 할 돈을 일부러 갚지 않고 모른 척할 때 써요. 돈이 없어서 늦게 갚는 것과 달리 나쁜 의도가 느껴져요. 줄여서 '떼먹다'라고도 해요. '빵을 조금 떼어 먹다'처럼 띄어 쓰면 말 그대로 떼어서 먹는 거예요.

phrases.en: You shouldn't stiff a friend out of their money.
phrases.nuance_ko: '떼어먹다'의 줄임말로 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The shortened form of '떼어먹다', more common in conversation.

phrases.en: The customer left without paying his tab.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에서 외상으로 산 값을 안 낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone doesn't pay what they owe on credit at a shop.
phrases.en_equiv: to skip out on a tab

phrases.en: The boss cheated the employees out of their wages.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄 돈을 일부러 주지 않는 나쁜 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the bad act of deliberately withholding pay owed.

explain_en: Used when someone deliberately refuses to repay money owed, such as debts, unpaid tabs, or wages. Unlike paying late because of no money, it implies bad intent. It can also be shortened to '떼먹다'. Written with a space, as in '빵을 조금 떼어 먹다', it literally describes tearing off a piece and eating it.

t90.ax: He stiffed me for my money and moved away.

examples.en: The department store started a bargain sale.
I bought a winter coat during the sale period.
Until when does this sale run?
It's a sale, so every shop is crowded.

examples.ko: 바겐세일 때는 반품이 안 되는 곳도 있어요.
examples.en: Some places don't accept returns during a sale.

examples.ko: 연말 바겐세일에 맞춰 신발을 사려고 해요.
examples.en: I plan to buy shoes during the year-end sale.

explain: 가격을 크게 낮추어 파는 세일을 말하며, 백화점이나 가게의 안내문에서 자주 봐요. 대화에서는 그냥 '세일'이라고만 해도 돼요. '세일하다'처럼 동사로 쓸 때는 '세일'을 써요.

phrases.en: The sale starts tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대화에서는 '바겐세일' 대신 '세일'이라고 더 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In conversation, people say '세일' more often than '바겐세일'.

phrases.en: This shop is having a bargain sale right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세일이 진행되고 있다는 안내에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to say a sale is going on.

phrases.en: The shoe store has a sale this week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사로 쓰면 '세일'을 써요. '바겐세일하다'는 잘 안 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For the verb, use '세일'; '바겐세일하다' is rarely said.

explain_en: It means a sale with large price cuts, and you often see it on notices at department stores and shops. In conversation, just '세일' is fine. When you need a verb, use '세일' as in '세일하다'.

examples.en: An expensive gift feels like a burden.
Tomorrow's presentation weighed on me too much.

examples.ko: 집값이 너무 부담되면 이사하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: If the housing cost is too much of a burden, moving is a good idea.
Please tell me ahead of time about anything that feels like a burden.
It's a lot of money for me, so I think it'll be a burden.
Let's eat something simple so the bill isn't a burden.

explain: '부담되다'는 돈이나 일, 마음이 무겁게 느껴질 때 써요. '부담스럽다'를 더 자주 말해요. 상대에게 '부담 갖지 마세요'라고 하면 신경 쓰지 말라는 따뜻한 인사예요.

phrases.en: An expensive gift feels like a burden.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부담되다'보다 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More commonly used than '부담되다'.

phrases.en: A price like this isn't a burden.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이나 돈이 무겁지 않다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something doesn't feel heavy, in money or in mind.

phrases.example: 부담 갖지 마세요. 천천히 해도 돼요.
phrases.en: Don't feel pressured. You can take your time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 마음을 편하게 해 주는 인사말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A kind phrase to put someone at ease.

explain_en: 부담되다 is used when money, work or feelings seem heavy. In Korean 부담스럽다 is said more often. '부담 갖지 마세요' to someone is a kind way of saying don't worry about it.

t90.ax: An expensive gift feels like a burden.

examples.en: The volunteer group quickly supplied daily necessities to the flood victims.
When you move, you have to buy the daily necessities first.
Toilet paper and soap are typical daily necessities.
Prices rose, so the cost of daily necessities is a burden.

examples.ko: 이 마트에서는 생활필수품을 한꺼번에 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: At this mart you can buy daily necessities all at once.

examples.ko: 비상 가방에 생활필수품 몇 가지를 챙겨 두세요.
examples.en: Keep a few daily necessities packed in your emergency bag.

explain: 살아가는 데 꼭 있어야 하는 물건을 말하고, 줄여서 '생필품'이라고도 해요. 재난 지원, 이사, 물가 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 꼭 필요하지 않은 '사치품'과 대비돼요.

phrases.example: 태풍 때문에 가게에 생필품이 다 떨어졌어요.
phrases.en: Because of the typhoon, the store ran out of daily necessities.
phrases.nuance_ko: '생활필수품'을 줄인 말로 뉴스와 대화에서 모두 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 생활필수품, common in news and conversation.

phrases.en: I buy daily necessities at the mart every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴지, 비누, 쌀처럼 꼭 필요한 물건을 살 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for buying must-have items like tissue, soap, or rice.

phrases.en: The disaster area is short of daily necessities.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재난이나 어려운 상황을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for disasters or hard situations.

explain_en: It means goods you must have to live, and it is often shortened to '생필품'. It appears in talk about disaster relief, moving and prices. It contrasts with '사치품' (luxury goods) that are not essential.
